solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not the principal allegiance temp is bound by at intervals

indicators.note: the letters from 'temp' sit tied up inside the word for allegiance

parts.note: duty is what you owe, your allegiance

indicators.note: take every other letter of 'temp'

parts.note: second and fourth letters of TEMP

explanation.surface: An office temp is caught between loyalty to the boss and to someone less senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temp' looks like the deputy itself, but it only supplies two letters; 'Not the principal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy acts for someone else and is not the principal.

clue.text: Make little of not working on stage show

parts.note: a system that is down is not working
a play is a show on stage

explanation.surface: Someone belittles a stage show that has stopped running.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts DOWN above PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to play something down is to minimise its importance.

clue.text: Each year, worry about relating to faithless people

parts.note: per annum, abbreviated PA

indicators.note: the word for worry is turned about

parts.note: to nag is to worry at someone

explanation.surface: Every year someone frets over people who have lost their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is 'per annum', Latin for each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan describes those outside the main faiths, seen as faithless.

clue.text: Secure draw

definitions.meaning: a verb: fasten with a knot
a noun: a match with no winner

explanation.surface: A team makes sure of a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are read as verbs in the surface; 'draw' is the noun, a tied result.
explanation.definitionFit: You tie a knot to secure it, and a match that ends level is a tie.

clue.text: No striking poet, but there may be some steel here

definitions.text: there may be some steel here

parts.note: a scab is a worker who will not join a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet refuses to join a strike, yet he has some steel in him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' suggests backbone; here it is a sword, which sits in a scabbard.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a steel blade.

clue.text: Start of career not so rich for office worker

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of CAREER
lean food is less rich

explanation.surface: Someone begins working life on poorer wages in an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office worker' suggests a clerk; it is the person who cleans the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Office cleaners work in offices after hours.

clue.text: Initiate pupils in vital course

parts.note: to blood a newcomer is to initiate them
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability

explanation.surface: Pupils are introduced to an essential school course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' reads as a school subject; here it is the course the blood flows, which is vital to life. In British schools pupils are grouped by ability into streams.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloodstream is the flowing course of blood, vital to life.

clue.text: Opponent of government is tense after seconds of fairly unpleasant teasing

indicators.note: take the second letter of each word

parts.note: second letters of FAIRLY and UNPLEASANT
arch means playfully teasing
used as it stands
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A rebel grows tense after a round of mildly nasty mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teasing' is not part of the letter selection; it gives ARCH as a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy means rule by no one, so its supporter is against any government at all.

clue.text: Make out drama's opening key lines

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of DRAMA
the Escape key on a keyboard
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: An actor works out the key lines at the start of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'lines' look like theatre words; one is a computer key, the other a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: to catch sight of something far off, as in making out a ship on the horizon.

clue.text: Ground seeds popular among staff

parts.note: a pole is a staff
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Some seeds have become fashionable with the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinole is a flour of ground seeds or grains, from Mexico and the American Southwest.

clue.text: Lover of composer's wit, broadcast entire

indicators.note: the letters of ENTIRE are scattered like seed

parts.note: a wag is a wit, a joker
ENTIRE rearranged

explanation.surface: A music lover repeats a composer's joke in full on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'has': the lover of the composer has WAG plus the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wagnerite is an enthusiast for Wagner's music.

clue.text: Medical procedure in addition cut stones

indicators.note: the word for 'in addition' loses its last letter

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation
ALSO without its last letter

explanation.surface: A surgeon also removes kidney stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut stones' sounds like gems or gallstones being cut; 'cut' works on ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the opal is one kind of gemstone, prized for its shifting colours.

clue.text: God with hooked fingers catches nothing in trousers

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
talons are hooked claws
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A clawed god grabs nothing in his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trousers' looks like where the nothing is caught; it is the definition, an adjective for someone wearing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloons are trousers, so pantalooned means wearing them.

clue.text: Turn up with cider unexpectedly: cheers!

indicators.note: the letters of CIDER come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive
CIDER rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone surprises the party by arriving with cider and raising a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' reads as a toast; it is the British informal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is Italian for goodbye, as 'cheers' is in British speech.

clue.text: I'm surprised fabulous bird has come from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of fable

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that a mythical bird has flown in from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Almost lost moisture out of doors in Scots town

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete: drop its last letter

parts.note: in the open air is out of doors
DRIED without its last letter

explanation.surface: Washing hung outside nearly dried in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order to the clue: AIR comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a town east of Glasgow in North Lanarkshire.

clue.text: Given inferior position on stage, very much resented losing top place

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, which goes

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a leg is a stage of a journey

parts.words: very much resented losing top place
parts.note: HATED without its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor pushed to the back of the stage bitterly resented being demoted from the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On stage' looks like theatre, but the two words are separate pieces, and a stage here is part of a journey. Relegation is what happens to a British football team that drops a division.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of teams demoted to a lower league and of people pushed to lesser jobs.

clue.text: Shop's business turning round after receiving international investment

indicators.note: the finished word is turned back to front
the word for after takes I in

parts.note: later means after
I for international, invested inside

explanation.surface: A store's trade picks up after foreign investment arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes in after the L of LATER to make LIATER, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail, selling to the public, is what a shop does.

clue.text: Disguising my age, end as top-rank waiter?

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged beyond recognition

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ageing waiter hides how old he is to see out his career at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-rank' is Olympus: Ganymede served wine to the gods, the highest company there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the cupbearer of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Working at last, really enjoyed having something on hand

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'working'

parts.note: last letter of WORKING
to love something is to really enjoy it

explanation.surface: Someone finally back at work loves having a task ready to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On hand' means available; here it is literal, something worn on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloved means wearing a glove, something on the hand.

clue.text: County lass has finished on top

parts.note: done means finished
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A country girl has come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards: the lass is below, 'finished' is on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Disinclination to move at home: it's about dividing time

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the two letters swap round

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the reversed pair splits the word for time into two parts

parts.note: an era is a period of time
used as it stands; the ’s that follows means 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone stays put at home, as time is split by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining the pieces: 'it is about, dividing time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from physics, where a body at rest resists being moved; in people it is sluggish unwillingness to act.

clue.text: Animals I live with upset relations

parts.note: used as it stands
to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: sexual relations

explanation.surface: Someone lives with animals and has fallen out with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives, but it is sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats.

clue.text: Like my phone? Old, black, not compact

parts.note: O is short for old
B for black, as on pencils
long is not compact

explanation.surface: Someone describes a phone as old, black and bulky.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: most phones are oblong.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone is a rectangle longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Slough left out of journal

parts.note: a blog is an online journal
L is short for left

explanation.surface: A word for marsh is missing from a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough, rhyming with 'cow', is a swamp, not the Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are soft, waterlogged ground, as in Bunyan's Slough of Despond.

clue.text: Extra pay from slaughtering enemy dragon?

indicators.note: the words are hacked apart and reassembled

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight claims a bonus for killing a hostile dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that dragon-slaying is just the sort of job that earns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for the bonus paid on top of wages for hazardous work.

clue.text: Innocent individual's first to occupy space for congregation

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'individual'

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church, where the congregation sits

indicators.note: the I moves into the word for the space

parts.note: first letter of INDIVIDUAL

explanation.surface: An innocent person is the first to take a seat in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space for congregation' could be any hall; the church sense is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone naive is artless and unworldly, as an innocent is.

clue.text: Swimmer got terrible cramps

indicators.note: the words cramp, confine, the answer within them

parts.note: gOT TERrible

explanation.surface: A swimmer suffered bad cramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramps' reads as a noun; it is the verb, to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the otter spends much of its life swimming in rivers and the sea.

clue.text: Syrup dispersed anger, peace finally after row

indicators.note: the letters of ANGER are scattered
after means following, so the letter from 'peace' is placed behind the word for row

parts.note: ANGER rearranged
a din is a loud row

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'peace'

parts.note: last letter of PEACE

explanation.surface: Something sweet calmed the anger and brought peace after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a noisy quarrel, rhyming with 'cow', not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red syrup flavoured with pomegranate.

clue.text: Each and everybody

definitions.meaning: the sense used in level scores, such as 'three apiece'

explanation.surface: Every single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each' fits ALL only in scores: 'three all' is three each.
explanation.definitionFit: All means everybody, and in scoring it means each.

clue.text: We hear Olympians, one and all, backed huge film star

indicators.note: the Olympians are said, not spelt

parts.note: the Olympians are the Greek gods
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters of 'all' are turned back

parts.note: used as it stands

explanation.surface: The athletes backed a big movie star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympians' suggests athletes; they are the gods on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the giant monster who stars in Japanese films.

clue.text: Hurry away from church in warm coat

parts.note: to flee is to hurry away
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out of church in a thick coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurry away from church' reads as one action, but it splits into two pieces; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a warm jacket of fleecy fabric, or a sheep's coat.
